chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Our love, [i.e., the love of] the Ahl al-Bayt, removes sins from the servants just as the strong wind removes leaves from the tree.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House, referring to the family of the Prophet Muhammad, particularly the Imams

ai.seo_question: How does loving the Ahl al-Bayt affect the sins of believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) describing the love for the Ahl al-Bayt as a powerful mechanism for expiation, likening it to a strong wind stripping leaves from a tree. This metaphor underscores the completeness and ease with which divine love purifies the believer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *mawadda* (affection) as a spiritual catalyst for forgiveness and closeness to God. The narration highlights that this love is not merely emotional but carries ontological weight in the cosmic order of salvation.
